answer: A newcomer key is an island until it finishes a live task assigned by a rotating peer panel. The panel hashes the output with that exact public key into a cipher, recomputes it, and countersigns only on a timely match. Only a sealed, key-bound cipher opens the haven of established payouts. A copied cipher fails the binding check, so a farm of a thousand aliases owes a thousand distinct attested jobs, while an honest agent pays that cost once.
